dedupe_keys.name: brtdata global database of bus rapid transit and bus priority systems

description: BRTData gathers information on bus priority systems in cities around the world, as a research source for academics, journalists, students and municipal technicians and as technical background for public transport decisions. It covers bus rapid transit systems (median-aligned segregated lanes, off-board fare collection and level boarding) and bus priority systems with dedicated lanes but without all BRT elements. Users can browse the systems and corridors of each city, compare indicators on design, performance and cost, and generate graphs. It was developed by the BRT+ Centre of Excellence and WRI with the Institute for Transportation and Development Policy, and the site says it is updated monthly with verified data. Coverage: cities worldwide with BRT or bus priority. Format and access: web tables and charts without registration. Licence and cost: free; no reuse licence is stated. Caveats: indicator completeness varies by city. It supports capacity planning and network flow studies of bus corridors. It relates to the National Transit Database in the catalogue.
